name: Academic Word List – Sublist 1
source: Headwords from A. Coxhead, “A New Academic Word List,” TESOL Quarterly, vol. 34, no. 2, pp. 213–238, 2000. Definitions and examples written for WordWise.

words.definition: A part of a place, or a particular subject or field of activity.
words.example: Her main area of research is renewable energy.

words.definition: Able to be used, obtained or reached.
words.example: The lecture slides are available on the subject website.

words.definition: An advantage or good result that something gives you.
words.example: One benefit of group study is hearing other points of view.

words.definition: To make something new exist.
words.example: The students created a survey to collect their data.

words.definition: Facts or numbers collected to be examined and used to make decisions.
words.example: The data show a steady rise in enrolments.

words.definition: The system of trade, industry and money in a country or region.
words.example: Tourism is an important part of the local economy.

words.definition: The natural world, or the conditions in which people live and work.
words.example: A quiet environment helps many students concentrate.

words.definition: To send goods to another country to sell them.
words.example: Australia exports large amounts of iron ore.

words.definition: The management of money, or the money needed for a plan.
words.example: The project failed because it lacked finance.

words.definition: Money received regularly from work or investments.
words.example: Many students rely on part-time work for their income.

words.definition: Relating to one person or thing, rather than a group.
words.example: Each student receives individual feedback on the essay.

words.definition: An important topic or problem that people discuss.
words.example: Privacy is a key issue in mobile app design.

words.definition: Work, especially physical work, or the workers who do it.
words.example: Machines have reduced the need for manual labour.

words.definition: Connected with the law, or allowed by the law.
words.example: The company sought legal advice before launching the app.

words.definition: Very large or important compared with others.
words.example: Climate change is a major challenge for coastal cities.

words.definition: A share of a total, measured in parts of one hundred.
words.example: Forty percent of respondents studied at night.

words.definition: A length of time.
words.example: The trial ran over a period of six weeks.

words.definition: A set of agreed plans or rules for action.
words.example: The university has a clear policy on late submissions.

words.definition: Careful study to discover new facts or information.
words.example: Their research compared two teaching methods.

words.definition: The function or position someone or something has.
words.example: Sleep plays an important role in memory.

words.definition: A way of dealing with a problem or task.
words.example: We took a step-by-step approach to the analysis.

words.definition: To judge the quality, size or value of something.
words.example: The quiz assesses how well you understood the reading.

words.definition: The power to make decisions, or an expert whose opinion is respected.
words.example: She is an authority on Australian history.

words.definition: A general idea or principle.
words.example: Recursion is a difficult concept for new programmers.

words.definition: To be made of particular parts (used with “of”).
words.example: The exam consists of three short essays.

words.definition: The situation or background that helps explain something.
words.example: Read the sentence in context to work out the meaning.

words.definition: A formal written agreement that can be enforced by law.
words.example: Read the contract carefully before you sign it.

words.definition: To state exactly what something means or what its limits are.
words.example: The first chapter defines the key terms.

words.definition: To share or spread something among people or places.
words.example: The tutor distributed the worksheets at the start.

words.definition: To start something lasting, or to show that something is true.
words.example: The study established a link between diet and mood.

words.definition: To make a careful guess about a size, amount or value.
words.example: We estimated the cost before buying the equipment.

words.definition: One of the things that causes or influences a result.
words.example: Cost was the main factor in their decision.

words.definition: The purpose or job of something.
words.example: The main function of the roots is to absorb water.

words.definition: To recognise or name someone or something.
words.example: The report identifies three risks to the project.

words.definition: A particular way of doing something.
words.example: The method section explains how the data were collected.

words.definition: To happen or exist.
words.example: Errors often occur when steps are skipped.

words.definition: A series of actions taken to achieve a result.
words.example: Writing is a process of drafting and revising.

words.definition: To need something, or to make it necessary.
words.example: The course requires weekly reading.

words.definition: To reply, or to react to something.
words.example: Participants responded to an online questionnaire.

words.definition: One of the parts that something is divided into.
words.example: Answer every question in section B.

words.definition: To examine something in detail to understand or explain it.
words.example: We analysed the interview transcripts for common themes.

words.definition: To accept something as true without proof.
words.example: The model assumes that prices stay constant.

words.definition: To form or make up something.
words.example: Women constitute half of the participants.

words.definition: To get or develop something from a source.
words.example: Many English words are derived from Latin.

words.definition: Clear and easy to see or understand.
words.example: It was evident from the results that the method worked.

words.definition: A rule or method written with symbols or numbers.
words.example: Use the formula to calculate the area of a circle.

words.definition: To show or suggest that something is true.
words.example: Early results indicate a small improvement.

words.definition: To decide what something means, or to explain its meaning.
words.example: Scholars interpret the poem in different ways.

words.definition: To include something as a necessary part.
words.example: The job involves analysing large data sets.

words.definition: To make laws.
words.example: Parliament legislated to protect consumers online.

words.definition: A basic rule or belief that guides behaviour or explains how something works.
words.example: Honesty is a core principle of professional practice.

words.definition: To continue, or to move on to the next step.
words.example: After the pilot study, the team proceeded with the full trial.

words.definition: One part of a country’s economy or of society.
words.example: Jobs in the health sector are growing quickly.

words.definition: Large or important enough to have an effect or be noticed.
words.example: There was a significant difference between the two groups.

words.definition: Alike, but not exactly the same.
words.example: The two studies reached similar conclusions.

words.definition: Where something comes from, such as a book or person giving information.
words.example: Always cite the source of a quotation.

words.definition: Particular and clearly defined.
words.example: Set a specific goal for each study session.

words.definition: The way the parts of something are arranged or organised.
words.example: A clear structure makes an essay easier to follow.

words.definition: A set of ideas intended to explain something.
words.example: The theory explains why spaced practice improves recall.

words.definition: To be different, or to change, in different situations.
words.example: Reading speeds vary widely between students.
